application_type_full: Tree works: Trees in conservation areas/subject to TPOs
description: TPO 195 T1 1x Oak ground works and associated fibrous root pruning to install/ extend a root barrier 15m in length and 3m in depth.
decision_conditions: The removal of deadwood, dangerous / hanging branches and ivy:  This does not require the formal consent of the Council.

Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981:  Note that it is an offence under this act to disturb roosting bats, nesting birds or any other protected species.  Therefore, if applicable, it is advisable to consult your tree surgeon / consultant to agree an acceptable time for carrying out the approved works.
Owner(s)'s permission:  Permission should be sought from the owner(s) of the tree(s) and / or the owner(s) of the land that the tree(s) overhang prior to any approved work being carried out.

Expected standard of tree work: The approved works must be carried out in accordance with the conditions laid out above. If they are not, then enforcement action could being taken which could lead to prosecution and heavy fines. Therefore, it is highly recommended that the works are only carried out by a professional and competent arboriculturist who undertakes to comply with the conditions of this consent and in accordance with industry best practice (BS 3998:2010).

The Arboricultural Association can provide details of its approved contractors, who have demonstrated such professionalism and competence, on their website (www.trees.org.uk) or by calling 01242 522152. Or on request the Council can provide a list of contractors who are known to carry out tree work to a good standard and to normally maintain an appropriate policy of indemnity insurance.

All excavation works associated with the installation of the root barrier within the root protection area of the protected Oak shall be undertaken by hand using non-percussive tools only. No mechanical excavation shall take place unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Root disturbance and severance shall be kept to the absolute minimum necessary to install the approved root barrier.

No roots exceeding 25mm in diameter shall be cut without the prior written approval of the London Borough of Hillingdon. All roots shall be cleanly pruned using sharp tools, and any exposed roots shall be suitably protected to prevent desiccation during the works.
Should any large, significant, or buttress roots be encountered, works shall cease immediately, and the London Borough of Hillingdon shall be notified to agree an appropriate method of proceeding.
